chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:
"If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has no need for a servant, He tests him with miserliness."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, meaning the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.ابْتَلَاهُ: He tested him; referring to a trial or affliction from Allah
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: The servant or human being in relation to Allah
key_terms.بِالْبُخْلِ: With miserliness; stinginess as the specific moral trial mentioned
key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: A need; here referring to divine regard or purpose concerning the servant
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For Allah; indicating the divine will and relation to the servant

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali عليه السلام say about miserliness as a trial from Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents miserliness as a divine trial and a sign of a servant's spiritual deprivation. It warns against stinginess and highlights the moral importance of generosity in one's relationship with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1717 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"If Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has no need for a servant, He tests him with miserliness."
